Commentary.Commentary: After an ordinary performance with the ball in the previous two session, their skipper stepped up and took 4 wickets. He was well supported by Sandakan and Lakmal. Now, can the Lankans bounce back? Or will the Tigers make full use of their lead? Join us soon to find back!

Shakib then carried his team and along with the debutant, Mosaddek Hossain took his team past Sri Lanka's total. He got to his 5th Test ton while Hossain scored his maiden fifty. The debutant played a crucial role and added valuable runs with the lower order batsmen.

Bangladesh have emerged on top and taken a healthy lead of 129 runs! The openers once again gave them a superb start. But once they departed, they saw a mini-collapse in the last session of day 2. Mushfiqur Rahim and Shakib Al Hasan then steadied the ship. The former scored a half century before getting out to a superb delivery from Suranga Lakmal.

Day 3... Session 3...

The wicket is still a good one to bat and Bangladesh will aim to continue their good work and put more pressure on the hosts. They already have a 90-run lead which could be more than handy on this surface. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will be disappointed with their work despite the wicket of Shakib towards Tea. They have not looked threatening apart from Sandakan. Herath will hope they can wrap the innings up early and ensure they are not conceding a huge lead. Promises to be an exciting last session of play. Do join us in a while for it.

The pair of Shakib and Mosaddek Hossain shared the highest seventh wicket stand against Sri Lanka in Sri Lanka to get right on top of the game. Mosaddek especially has shown tremendous resolve to register his maiden Test fifty.

Rahim went onto score his 17th half century and was looking set for more. However, the second new ball yielded a positive result for the home side as Lakmal foxed Rahim with a good in-swinger to rattle his stumps. But Shakib has carried on and is batting well. He has gone past his fifty and along with the lower order will look to move ahead of Sri Lanka's score to take a crucial lead. Will the hosts be able to bowl out the visitors cheaply? Join us to find out in a while.

Pitch Report - Russel Arnold doing the report reckons that there are roughs on the wicket which are starting to open up. He adds that the deck is on the slower side and hence the shot selection is vital. Mentions that the wear and tear will only increase.

The deficit for the visitors is still a healthy 124 runs, with the pitch still being good to bat on, they will hope the pair of Shakib Al Hasan and Mushfiqur Rahim bat long and take them to parity. Any form of lead on this wicket will be a handy one and on what is usually a moving day in the Test, Day 3 holds a lot of answers to the future of this Test. Stay tuned for all the action.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of Day 3 of the second and final Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh at P Sara Oval, Colombo. The hosts came back in the game in the final session on Day 2 taking four wickets to peg the visitors back who had begun well. Lakshan Sandakan was tough to pick and the Lankans will hope that he can continue to weave his magic over Bangladesh.
Day 3... Session 1...

Sri Lanka will be happy with their work, things looked very gloomy for them before they took three wickets in the last half an hour to get the control back. Lakshan Sandakan was the best bowler for them, as all the Bangladesh batsmen struggled to pick him. He will hope for more support from his teammates as they will know that any lead on this surface could be handy. The visitors will aim to get as close to Sri Lanka's total as possible first and then take the game from there. There is a lot at stake, do join us for all the action on Day 3 tomorrow at 1000 local (0430 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and take care!

Just as they say one brings two, Bangladesh lost the plot of the Test to an extent, going from 192 for 2 to 198 for 5. Taijul, the nightwatchman bagged a golden duck and Lakmal bounced out Sabbir who played well for 42. Shakib - playing a shot every ball, managed to see the day through, courtesy of a drop. The visitors still trail by 124 runs and they will know they have a lot of work left to be done.

The Bangladesh openers in Tamim Iqbal and Soumya Sarkar shared a fine opening stand of 95 runs to give them the platform. Tamim departed for 49 but Sarkar ensured he got to his half century. He though fell soon after to Sandakan. Just when Imrul Kayes and Sabbir Rahman were starting to put pressure back on the hosts with a 62-run stand, the former missed a straight one and was dismissed lbw.

A brilliant day of Test cricket! Sri Lanka have finished the game on top. They started well, scoring 100 runs in the first session with Dinesh Chandimal registering his fourth Test ton against Bangladesh. The hosts would have hoped to keep pressure on the visitors but that was not the case.

The throw at the striker's end hits the woodwork and ricochets away. Shakib wants a run for an overthrow but the umpire signals that the ball has become dead. Coming back to the shot, what a poor choice of shot it was from Shakib. Especially, when his side was in so much of trouble.

Once again he got the start but couldn't convert it into a big one!

The replays show that Kayes grounded his foot in time. Good work from both the batsman as well as the keeper!

4th Test fifty for Soumya Sarkar!

FIFTY FOR SARKAR! He played with fire there! Off spinner, pitched outside off, spinning away, Sarkar waits for the ball to spin and then guides it just past first slip, who dives to his left but fails to get hand to the ball. Three runs taken! Sarkar continues his good work in the series!

Fuller one outside off, pushed through cover-point for a single.
Spinning in from outside off, defended from within the crease.
FOUR! Innovation! Served outside off, Kayes brings out his reverse sweeps and gets it through third man for a boundary. He is trying to take the charge to Herath!
SUPERB DELIVERY! Tossed up outside off, draws Sarkar forward to defend. Sarkar obliges and presses forward to defend but the ball spins away sharply with extra bounce. A classical off spinner!

We are back for the final session of play. SOUMYA SARKAR will continue his innings and IMRUL KAYES joins him in the middle. RANGANA HERATH to continue his over. Here we go...
...DAY 2, SESSION 3...

Tamim got a couple of chances when two marginal decisions went his way. The third one didn't go his way as Herath struck to trap him in front. Bangladesh though have done well, the trail is still 243 runs. Sri Lanka will want to come back hard after Tea and ensure they are on top of the game by taking wickets at regular intervals. Promises to be an interesting session. Join us in a while for it.

A good session for Bangladesh! They would have been under pressure after a poor first session with the ball but have come back well with a fine opening stand which was broken only at the stroke of Tea. Both the openers had their nervy moments. Sarkar in particular though has been pretty solid.

OUT! REVIEW SUCCESSFUL! Tamim misses out on another fifty by just one run. Quicker one and fullish in length on off, slides in with the arm. Iqbal looks to play it across but misses and is rapped on the front pad. There is a huge appeal for LBW but the umpire is not interested. Herath decides to take the review this time. Time for the replays. They do not spot any inside edge. The Hawk Eye shows that the impact is in line and it is going to crash into the leg stump. The decision has to be overturned and fortunately for Sri Lanka, they made the right call to go for the review and get the correct decision. THAT SHALL BE TEA ON DAY 2!
